This model examines how age (a proxy for things that happen over time) influences spoken words ($A \rightarrow S$).

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
```

## Statistical model

We model the number of words spoken as a bounded count outcome out of an 810-word reference inventory. The expected proportion of words spoken is modelled as a smooth function of age. On the logit scale, this function is the sum of a linear developmental trend and a Gaussian process term that allows flexible nonlinear departures from linearity. To account for extra variation between children beyond that expected under a simple binomial model, we use a Beta-Binomial likelihood. The Beta-Binomial dispersion parameter is also allowed to vary with age, so the degree of heterogeneity may change over development. Wordbank WG, Oxford CDI, and Words & Sentences rows contribute spoken observations. Priors for the linear trend are specified indirectly through the expected proportion of words spoken at two reference ages, making the prior assumptions more interpretable.

::: {.callout-note title="Model at a glance"}

- **Population:** typically developing children.
- **Outcome:** words spoken out of the common 810-word reference inventory.
- **Age anchors:** 12 and 26 months.
- **Data handling:** 25% TD subsample; Wordbank WG, Oxford CDI, and Words & Sentences rows contribute spoken observations.
- **Role in the model family:** baseline TD spoken trajectory; VG11 is the full-data study-random-effect successor.

:::

::: {.callout-note}

For full details and discussion, please refer to the technical report.

## Priors

The TD anchor ages are much younger than the DS anchor ages because typical spoken vocabulary changes rapidly across the second year. The low-age anchor is near the floor at 12 months, while the 26-month anchor mildly favours larger vocabularies but remains broad on the 810-word scale. The GP and `kappa` priors match the shared univariate model machinery.

## Prior predictive checks

Read these checks as a pre-data plausibility test over the TD age range: simulated spoken counts should be low near 9-12 months, capable of rapid growth by 24-30 months, and not mechanically pinned to the inventory ceiling.

## Posterior predictions

The main findings to inspect are the spoken trajectory and its cross-sectional age derivative across the TD age window. Use VG11 when the question requires the full TD data pool and dataset-level variation.

### Posterior summary table for selected ages

In this model, $p$ is the latent success probability -- the underlying proportion of the vocabulary checklist a child is expected to produce at a given age. $Ey$ is the expected value implied by the latent mean $p$. It reflects uncertainty in the mean developmental trajectory. $Y$ is a draw from the posterior predictive distribution. It reflects both uncertainty in the mean trajectory and extra-binomial variability (dispersion).

```{python}
posterior_summary = pd.read_csv("posterior_summary.csv", index_col=0)
posterior_summary
```

### Posterior predictive probability mass function (PMF) for word counts, by age

### Posterior predictive cumulative distribution function (CDF) for word counts, by age

### Cross-sectional age derivative

The posterior distribution of the derivative of expected spoken words with respect to age, in words per month. This is a cross-sectional derivative of the fitted age trajectory, not a within-child learning rate. The uncertainty bands show how the derivative varies across posterior draws of $f$.

![expected_learning_rate](expected_learning_rate.png){#fig-expected-learning-rate .lightbox fig-align="left"}

### Posterior distribution for dispersion parameter $\kappa$

Lower $\kappa$ values indicate greater overdispersion (greater between-child variability relative to the mean), while higher $\kappa$ values indicate less overdispersion (less between-child variability relative to the mean). The plot shows how the estimated dispersion parameter $\kappa$ changes with age, along with uncertainty intervals.

![posterior_kappa](posterior_kappa.png){#fig-posterior-kappa .lightbox fig-align="left"}
